reference_drawer.title: 📖 Tangent-Radius Theorem Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Essential theorems for tangents, radii, chords and tangent angles.

items.rule: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
After establishing the right angle at P, use Pythagoras.
items.example: Use the positive root for a length.

items.rule: A radius to the tangency point is perpendicular to the outer-circle chord and bisects the chord.
items.example: Use the inner radius as the perpendicular distance from O to AB.

items.rule: The angle between two tangents is supplementary to the central angle between the radii to the contact points.
items.example: This follows from the two radius-tangent right angles.

concepts.title: 1. Tangent-Radius Perpendicularity
concepts.subtitle: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at contact
concepts.summary: If PT is tangent to a circle at P and O is the center, then OP is perpendicular to PT. This creates a right triangle OPT.

points.text: At the point of contact P, use $OP\perp PT$.
Therefore $\angle OPT=90^\circ$ and Pythagoras applies in $\triangle OPT$.

concepts.title: 2. Angles in Triangle OPT
concepts.subtitle: Use the fixed right angle and triangle sum
concepts.summary: The tangent-radius theorem fixes the angle at P as 90°. The remaining two angles in triangle OPT are therefore complementary.

concepts.title: 3. Concentric Circles and Tangent Chord
concepts.subtitle: The inner radius becomes the center-to-chord distance
concepts.summary: A chord of the larger circle tangent to the smaller circle is perpendicular to the inner radius at the tangency point. Pythagoras gives the half-chord.

concepts.title: 4. Angle Between Two Tangents
concepts.subtitle: Central angle and tangent angle are supplementary
concepts.summary: The radii to the two contact points are perpendicular to their tangents, so the angle between the two tangents and the central angle add to 180°.

schema_notes.atomic_progression: Pythagoras questions: state perpendicularity → state Pythagoras → substitute values → simplify and solve. Angle questions: establish 90° → use triangle sum → substitute → solve. Concentric-circle questions: tangency perpendicularity → Pythagoras → find half-chord → double. Two-tangent questions: establish two right angles → quadrilateral sum → substitute central angle → solve.
schema_notes.strict_options_rule: Every strategy option and option_details text combines a brief geometric/algebraic instruction with actual mathematical content, and all formulas, values and equations are wrapped in single dollar signs.
schema_notes.svg_rule: Every pool question contains a mandatory responsive SVG using viewBox 0 0 280 180; diagrams depict the required circle, radius, tangent, chord or two-tangent geometry.
schema_notes.latex_compliance: All equations, worked examples and rubric mathematics use multiline aligned LaTeX with at most one equals sign per line.
schema_notes.guided_calculation_compliance: Every step has exactly two vertically stacked outputs and every field uses placeholder Enter value; prompts and field labels do not reveal answers or intermediate expressions.
schema_notes.pool_compliance: Each of the four typologies contains exactly 12 unique questions: 4 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.
